lesson_scope: Solving trigonometric equations involving R-form expressions in degrees and radians with phase shifts and scaled arguments.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving basic Rcos(theta - alpha) = c equation in degrees across [0, 360].

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Inverting R-form cosine equation to find roots in standard degree interval.

hints: Divide by $5$ to isolate the cosine term: $\cos(\theta - 53.13^\circ) = \frac{2.5}{5} = 0.5$.
Find the principal angle: $\arccos(0.5) = 60^\circ$. The second angle in $[0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ is $360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Find valid angles within this domain:
$$\theta - 53.13^\circ = 60^\circ \implies \theta = 113.13^\circ \approx 113.1^\circ$$
$$\theta - 53.13^\circ = 300^\circ \implies \theta = 353.13^\circ \approx 353.1^\circ$$
$$\theta = 113.1^\circ, \ 353.1^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $\cos(\theta - 53.13^\circ) = 0.5$ and finds at least one valid angle for $\theta - 53.13^\circ$ (e.g. $60^\circ$ or $300^\circ$).
Obtains $\theta = 113.1^\circ$ and $\theta = 353.1^\circ$ and no other solutions in $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving Rsin(x + alpha) = c equation in radians with exact values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exact radian solving of sine R-form equation.

hints: Determine the domain for $x + \frac{\pi}{3}$: since $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, $\frac{\pi}{3} \le x + \frac{\pi}{3} \le \frac{7\pi}{3}$.
Identify solutions for $x + \frac{\pi}{3}$: $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ and $\frac{13\pi}{6}$. Subtract $\frac{\pi}{3}$ from each.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate the sine term and establish the domain:
$$2\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 1 \implies \sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$0 \le x \le 2\pi \implies \frac{\pi}{3} \le x + \frac{\pi}{3} \le \frac{7\pi}{3}$$

Find angles in the transformed domain where $\sin\phi = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$x + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{6} \implies x = \frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{3\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{2}$$
$$x + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{13\pi}{6} \implies x = \frac{13\pi}{6} - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{11\pi}{6}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains exact roots $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x = \frac{11\pi}{6}$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving R-form equation with negative constant in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Inversion with negative constant value.

hints: The angles where cosine is $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ in this range are $135^\circ$ and $225^\circ$. Subtract $45^\circ$ from each.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $\theta = 90^\circ$ and $\theta = 180^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving double-angle R-form sine equation in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Double angle argument with phase shift in R-form.

hints: Find angles: $2\theta - 36.87^\circ = 36.87^\circ$ and $2\theta - 36.87^\circ = 180^\circ - 36.87^\circ = 143.13^\circ$. Add $36.87^\circ$ and divide by $2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $\theta = 36.9^\circ$ and $\theta = 90.0^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving R-form equation in radians over symmetric interval [-pi, pi].

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving in symmetric radian interval [-pi, pi].

hints: Because cosine is symmetric, $x - 0.5 = \pm\frac{\pi}{3}$. Add $0.5$ to each root to obtain $x = -0.547$ and $x = 1.55$ rad.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate cosine and find domain:
$$\cos(x - 0.5) = 0.5$$
$$-\pi \le x \le \pi \implies -3.64 \le x - 0.5 \le 2.64$$

Find values of $x - 0.5$ within this domain:
$$x - 0.5 = \frac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.0472 \implies x = 0.5 + 1.0472 = 1.5472 \approx 1.55$$
$$x - 0.5 = -\frac{\pi}{3} \approx -1.0472 \implies x = 0.5 - 1.0472 = -0.5472 \approx -0.547$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $x = -0.547$ and $x = 1.55$ rad and no other solutions in $-\pi \le x \le \pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving boundary case of R-form equation where cos = 1.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Maximum value boundary condition solving.

hints: The only value in this interval where cosine equals $1$ is $360^\circ$. Subtract $33.69^\circ$ to find $\theta = 326.3^\circ$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $\theta = 326.3^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: classic R-form expression in degrees and subsequent equation solving.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Standard R-form conversion in degrees.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and equate coefficients with $4\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta$:
$$R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = R\cos\theta\cos\alpha + R\sin\theta\sin\alpha$$
$$R\cos\alpha = 4, \quad R\sin\alpha = 3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving R-form equation across [0, 360].

hints: Find both angles: $\theta - 36.87^\circ = 66.42^\circ$ and $\theta - 36.87^\circ = 360^\circ - 66.42^\circ = 293.58^\circ$. Add $36.87^\circ$ to each.

walkthrough.text:
Find valid angles in the domain $[-36.87^\circ, 323.13^\circ]$:
$$\text{Principal value: } \theta - 36.87^\circ = \arccos(0.4) \approx 66.42^\circ$$
$$\text{Second angle: } \theta - 36.87^\circ = 360^\circ - 66.42^\circ = 293.58^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds both angles $\theta - 36.87^\circ = 66.42^\circ$ and $\theta - 36.87^\circ = 293.58^\circ$ in domain $[-36.87^\circ, 323.13^\circ]$.
Obtains $\theta = 103.3^\circ$ and $\theta = 330.5^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: R-form sine conversion in radians and solving in [0, 2pi].

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: R-form sine expansion in radians.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and equate coefficients with $5\sin x - 12\cos x$:
$$R\sin(x - \alpha) = R\sin x\cos\alpha - R\cos x\sin\alpha$$
$$R\cos\alpha = 5, \quad R\sin\alpha = 12$$

State the resulting form:
$$5\sin x - 12\cos x \equiv 13\sin(x - 1.1760)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $\tan\alpha = \frac{12}{5}$ from expanding $R\sin(x - \alpha) = R\sin x\cos\alpha - R\cos x\sin\alpha$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving sine R-form equation across [0, 2pi].

hints: Find both angles: $x - 1.1760 = \frac{\pi}{6} \approx 0.5236$ and $x - 1.1760 = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6} \approx 2.6180$. Add $1.1760$ to each.

walkthrough.text:
Find valid angles in the domain $[-1.1760, 5.1072]$:
$$x - 1.1760 = \frac{\pi}{6} \approx 0.5236$$
$$x - 1.1760 = \frac{5\pi}{6} \approx 2.6180$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds both angles $x - 1.1760 = \frac{\pi}{6}$ and $x - 1.1760 = \frac{5\pi}{6} \approx 2.6180$ in domain $[-1.1760, 5.1072]$.
Obtains $x = 1.70$ and $x = 3.79$ rad and no other solutions in range.

$$R\cos\alpha = \sqrt{7}, \quad R\sin\alpha = 3$$

hints: Find angles: $2\theta + 48.59^\circ = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$ and $2\theta + 48.59^\circ = 180^\circ + 60^\circ = 240^\circ$. Subtract $48.59^\circ$ and divide by $2$.

$$2\theta + 48.59^\circ = 240^\circ$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: rational fraction extrema using R-form and subsequent reciprocal equation solving.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: R-form conversion used to find bounds of reciprocal fraction.

hints: For extrema of $\frac{1}{3\cos(\theta - 48.19^\circ) + 4}$: maximum occurs when $\cos = -1$ (giving $\frac{1}{1} = 1$) and minimum occurs when $\cos = 1$ (giving $\frac{1}{7}$).

walkthrough.text:
Determine maximum and minimum values:
$$\text{Maximum when } \cos(\theta - 48.19^\circ) = -1: \quad f_{\max} = \frac{1}{3(-1) + 4} = 1$$
$$\text{Minimum when } \cos(\theta - 48.19^\circ) = 1: \quad f_{\min} = \frac{1}{3(1) + 4} = \frac{1}{7}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains maximum value $1$ when denominator is minimum ($3(-1) + 4 = 1$).
Obtains minimum value $\frac{1}{7}$ when denominator is maximum ($3(1) + 4 = 7$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving rational fraction equation using R-form.
